newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai ministry recommends delay of second airport.
newsitem.headline: Thai ministry recommends delay of second airport.

text.p: Thailand's Transport and Communications Ministry has recommended the controversial $4 billion Nong Ngu Hao airport project be delayed, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.

The ministry had been charged with recommending on the fate of the on-again, off-again project for Bangkok's second airport. The cabinet will discuss the recommendation this morning and is expected to make a final decision.
"The study showed that the Nong Ngu Hao project needs to be adjusted and delayed," spokesman Sunai Junlapongsathorn told Reuters.
The ministry had conducted a three-week study on the project, which would be located in the eastern outskirts of Bangkok.

The spokesman said it had also recommended to the cabinet that 10 billion baht ($400 million) be spent on expanding the existing Don Muang Bangkok airport to make up for services that might be hit by the delay in the other project.
Dong Muang airport sits on land owned by the Royal Thai Air Force.
The Nong Ngu Hao project, first initiated in 1967, has made little progess since 1987 and has already been hit by heavy cost overruns and delays.
It was due to be opened for service in 2000, but was now expected to be delayed until 2002 or 2003, according to ministry sources.
"The study was clearly shown that after expanding Don Maung airport it would be capable of faciliating up to 40 million passengers annually up to the year 2007," the spokesman said.
Since Don Muang could have the capacity to cope with the passenger throughput for about the next 10 years, there was no need to rush to build the second airport, saving a lot of money, he added.
